tolerance: Every angle and irradiance is graded against the NREL SPA (pvlib.solarposition.spa_python) and the published closed forms named in the citations. The per-case tolerance is not chosen by hand: it is the spread the two independent solar-position references (NREL SPA and the Michalsky/NOAA ephemeris of pvlib.solarposition.ephemeris) themselves produce, propagated through the whole chain by re-running the reference with the declination and equation of time shifted by that spread (floor 0.01 deg in declination, 0.10 min in the equation of time, 2e-9 relative) and, independently, by the disagreement between the two published Earth-Sun distance formulations pvlib offers (NREL and Spencer 1971), which is about 1e-3 relative and enters every irradiance linearly. Typical values are 0.02 deg on sun elevation and 0.1-0.4 % on the irradiances, growing where the sun is low because the chain is stiff there. Bookkeeping identities (absorbed = absorptance x incident, components summing to the incident power, effective POA x area = incident power, net heat = 0 at the stagnation temperature) are exact arithmetic and are held to 1e-12 relative. The beam collecting area is compared against the tool's DECLARED bilinear interpolation on its 49 x 721 (declination, hour angle) table, reproduced independently here from exact closed-form projected areas; the difference between that table value and the exact projected area is reported per case as "discretisation" and never hidden - it is below 0.010 % for every case with the sun above 3 deg and reaches 0.11 % at a sun elevation of 1.6 deg.
not_benchmarked: The NASA POWER climatology itself is third-party data, not physics: the harness blocks the request so every case runs on the bundled offline grid, and one dedicated case checks that the online branch is taken when the request succeeds.
The monthly clearness index, Linke turbidity and the diffuse-fraction calibration are empirical inputs read from that climatology; they are passed to the reference as inputs and are not graded.

The Erbs, Perez, Ineichen-Perez, Martin-Ruiz, Brandemuehl-Beckman, Berdahl-Martin and Faiman relations are empirical correlations with published scatter. They are checked for faithful implementation and for being applied inside their stated range, not against measurements.
The day, month and year integrations (trapezoidal, 15-minute steps) are not separately benchmarked against an independent quadrature.

The ray-traced self-shading and sky/ground view factors of the non-convex shapes (recessed window with a recess, open box, bowl) are a Monte-Carlo-like hemispherical quadrature; only the convex shapes, whose aperture factors have closed forms, are graded here.
The tool's calendar is fixed to the year 2025, so leap-year date handling is not reachable through the interface and is not benchmarked.
run_notes: Driven through the DOM with Playwright/Chromium; values read back from Diagram.record.build(), the tool's own declared output surface.
The clear-sky scenario is used wherever the point is the radiative model, so that no empirical monthly clearness index enters the graded quantity.

Cross-check: this file's own Perez 1990 transposition agrees with pvlib.irradiance.perez to 5e-16 relative over the 32 plane cases; the two solar-position references agree to the spread quoted per case.
crosscheck: pvlib.irradiance.perez vs. the independent Perez implementation in gen_solargaincalculator.py: max 4.8e-16 relative over 32 cases. pvlib.solarposition.spa_python vs. pvlib.solarposition.ephemeris: the per-case declination and equation-of-time spread recorded in each case as solpos_spread.

Clear-sky GHI must decrease monotonically as the sun descends. The Ineichen-Perez enhancement term exp(0.01*m^1.8) grows faster than the extinction term falls once the air mass exceeds about 15, so the unclamped correlation turns back upwards near the horizon; this checks the declared air-mass cap of 12 removes that.

The photovoltaic model must lose efficiency as the cell heats up (gamma < 0) and the cell temperature must follow Faiman (2008) T_cell = T_air + POA/(u0 + u1*v) with the open-rack coefficients u0 = 25 W/m2K, u1 = 6.84 W/m3sK used by pvlib.temperature.faiman.
The stagnation temperature is defined by Q_abs = Q_rad + Q_conv. Setting the working surface temperature to the reported stagnation temperature must drive the reported net heat to zero.

network_access must be "external" and name the host, the page must load no third-party script/link/img, the tool must produce a complete result with the POWER request blocked, and it must switch to the POWER climatology when the request succeeds.

manifest_network_access.note: The location panel queries the NASA POWER climatology API (power.larc.nasa.gov/api/temporal/climatology/point) with the latitude and longitude you enter and downloads monthly irradiance, temperature, wind and humidity climatology for that point. Nothing else is transmitted and no third-party script is loaded. The page renders immediately from the bundled 10-degree offline grid and upgrades to the POWER data when the request succeeds, so every result can also be produced with no network at all.

cases.note: The encoded state must restore byte-identical inputs and bit-identical outputs in a fresh page.
The ?lang= query parameter must select the tool UI language for all six catalogue languages.

provenance_note: Every reference value is recomputed by bench-src/ref/gen_solargaincalculator.py from the sources this artifact cites. That generator was re-run on 2026-10-15 with pvlib 0.16.1 and reproduced all 6 015 leaves of bench-src/ref/solargaincalculator_ref.json with no numeric difference; the single leaf that moved is the citation naming the pvlib version the corpus was first generated with (0.15.2). An earlier note on this artifact said the generator could not be re-run because pvlib was absent: that was a fact about the container of the day and not about the corpus.
